lines.text: Your phone is about to crash this plane.
lines.see: Tight on a phone glowing amber on a seat-back tray inside a dark cabin, slow push

lines.text: At least, that's what the announcement wants you to think.
lines.see: Pull back down the aisle: rows of seats, dozens of phones lighting up one by one

lines.text: Here's what really happens when you forget flight mode.
lines.see: Camera slides out through the window, wide shot of the airliner over a night landscape

lines.text: Up here, your phone isn't near one tower. It's above loads of them.
lines.see: Crane down under the plane: a field of cell towers, an amber range ring spreads over many of them

lines.text: So it keeps hopping between them, calling out to every one.
lines.see: Amber pulses shoot from the phone down to tower after tower, each lights as it is hit

lines.text: That's the real problem. Not the plane. The network on the ground.
lines.see: Dive to ground level among the towers, they flicker and glitch, the plane small overhead

lines.text: That's why America banned phones in the air. In 1991.
lines.see: Headline 1991 counts up, towers settle back to calm

lines.text: The plane? The FAA says most airliners can tolerate it.
lines.see: Crane back up to the plane, an amber shield shimmers around the fuselage and holds

lines.text: Worst case? Pilots hear a buzz in their headsets, like a mosquito.
lines.see: Fly into the cockpit, a pilot headset, an amber waveform buzzing beside it

lines.text: Europe already said yes. 5G on planes, through a tiny mast on board.
lines.see: Pull out to the cabin ceiling, a small mast lights, a beam rises to a satellite

lines.text: So is flight mode about safety, or just a rule from 1991?
lines.see: Back to the same phone on the tray (loop to frame 0), question headline, comment bubble

facts.claim: The FCC's ban on airborne cell phone use was adopted in 1991 because of the threat of harmful interference to terrestrial (ground) cellular networks
FCC rule 47 CFR 22.925: when an aircraft leaves the ground, cellular phones on board must be turned off

FAA: most commercial airplanes can tolerate radio interference signals from personal electronic devices; phones in airplane mode allowed in all phases of flight; voice calls still barred under FCC rules
An airline pilot (@perchpoint, TikTok) said phones searching for towers can put 'a really annoying buzz' in pilots' headsets, 'like a mosquito in my ear'; a nuisance, not a safety catastrophe
The European Commission's decision lets airlines offer 5G on planes through an onboard pico-cell, usually linked to the ground network by satellite

Phones at low altitude switch between towers as the plane moves; the FAA advisory circular cites the need 'to eliminate interference between ground-based cellular stations and airborne cellular devices'
